scope: Swift host runtime only; audit, no behavior change

authority.vmAndGuestObservation: VMManager.bootReady, mgmtReady, bootFailedReason from serial markers
authority.daemonConclusion: not justified by current evidence; foreground child is the lifecycle owner

components.name: VMManager
components.queue: main for VZ and serial timer

components.name: PortForwardManager
resources: one listener per published TCP port

components.name: CLI lifecycle
components.owner: invoking CLI process + spawned foreground child
components.queue: blocking CLI loop; child main run loop

sockets.staleCleanup: unlink only after connect probe fails; owned path removed by stopAll
unlink only after connect probe fails; owned path removed by stopAll
unlink after failed connect probe; cancel handler also unlinks
kernel flock release on process exit; pathname retained

timers.name: serial/readiness poll
timers.fallback: boot timeout fails and initiates shutdown

readiness.guestManagement: serial HARPOON_MGMT_READY stored by VMManager but not a Lifecycle gate
readiness.hostDocker: Unix socket existence/connect plus HARPOON_RUNNING log in statusSnapshot
readiness.vmExit: not directly observed after start; only VZ start failure and explicit shutdown are handled

failurePaths.partialStartup: build/config/start failure exits; bridge start failures are logged and do not force FAILED or roll back already-started bridges
failurePaths.abruptHostCrash: OS closes FDs and releases flock; socket pathnames can remain stale and are cleaned on next bridge start; pid/json may remain for status cleanup
failurePaths.unexpectedVmExit: no dedicated VZ delegate/state transition path found; readiness/status may remain inferred from stale metadata until probes fail
failurePaths.restart: stop sends SIGTERM and stop file, waits 10s, waits for socket/lock disappearance, then starts; no force kill
failurePaths.staleState: dead/non-Harpoon PID metadata is removed; stale Unix sockets are connect-probed then unlinked; lock pathname is not removed

classifications: GOOD_BOUNDARY_KEEP: Docker/containerd/runc remain guest-owned and are reached through the host boundary
DUPLICATED_AUTHORITY_REVIEW: Lifecycle state, VMManager booleans, log markers, PID/lock/socket probes all describe overlapping readiness/liveness
IMPLICIT_OWNERSHIP_REVIEW: active per-connection FDs and VZ connections are local closures, not represented in BridgeSet registries
BLOCKING_IO_REVIEW: serial Data(contentsOf:), status probes, Process.waitUntilExit, and first-request translation can block main or global queues
LIFECYCLE_COUPLING_REVIEW: main.swift owns signal/timer/VM shutdown while BridgeSet owns resource cleanup
HISTORICAL_OR_DEAD_CANDIDATE_REMOVE: legacy single host-forward fields and unreachable _legacy_startHostPortForward are retained but unused
LIFECYCLE_COUPLING_REVIEW: BridgeSet.startAll has no aggregate result, so bridge bind failures can coexist with RUNNING
DUPLICATED_AUTHORITY_REVIEW: RuntimeConfig socket paths can diverge from fixed HarpoonPaths CLI/status probes
IMPLICIT_OWNERSHIP_REVIEW: socket mode checks are permissive in source even though live sockets were observed as 0600
BLOCKING_IO_REVIEW: nonblocking proxy writes busy-wait on EAGAIN
